content.value_statement: Portfolio Buddy feature work can drift into risky refactors or mobile gaps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to plan conservative, responsive changes.
actual_capabilities: Defines preservation-first rules for feature work and refactoring decisions.
Provides criteria for proposing high-value improvements with user approval.
Requires responsive Tailwind planning for mobile and desktop layouts.
Supplies a clarifying question format with options, pros, cons, and recommendations.
Shows Portfolio Buddy examples for financial metrics, state defaults, and responsive buttons.
limitations: Focused on Portfolio Buddy 2, so examples may need adaptation for other projects.
Does not run tests, inspect repositories, or enforce code quality by itself.
Does not replace product requirements, security review, or architecture approval.
Assumes Tailwind and React-style patterns for many UI examples.

use_cases.title: Plan a safe feature change
use_cases.description: Use the guide to preserve working code, identify risks, and request approval before larger changes.

use_cases.title: Check responsive design choices
use_cases.description: Apply the mobile and desktop checklist before adding UI controls, spacing, or visibility rules.

use_cases.title: Standardize requirement gathering
use_cases.description: Use the clarifying question format to compare options and explain trade-offs before implementation starts.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a small fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a low-risk change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the planning guidelines to plan this small Portfolio Buddy fix: [describe fix]. Preserve existing behavior and list mobile checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare clarification options
prompt_templates.scenario: Requirements are unclear or have several valid interpretations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the clarifying question format for this request: [describe request]. Give recommended and alternate options with trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an improvement exception
prompt_templates.scenario: A better implementation may require changing existing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether this proposed improvement meets the low-risk, high-upside, low-complexity criteria: [describe improvement].

prompt_templates.title: Create a full implementation plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning before a feature or refactor.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Portfolio Buddy implementation plan for [feature]. Include preservation strategy, responsive behavior, approval points, risks, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a new dashboard control for starting capital.
output_examples.output: A concise plan that extends the existing input, checks mobile touch targets, and asks whether the control should appear conditionally.

output_examples.input: Decide whether to replace a working calculation module.
output_examples.output: An exception analysis that compares risk, upside, complexity, and approval needs before recommending preservation or targeted change.

output_examples.input: Prepare questions for ambiguous trading day logic.
output_examples.output: A structured clarification with recommended and alternate interpretations, including pros, cons, and domain reasoning.

best_practices: Start by identifying existing code that should be preserved.
Check mobile and desktop behavior before calling a plan complete.
Ask one clear clarification when requirements affect architecture or user experience.
anti_patterns: Replacing working code because a different pattern looks cleaner.
Adding libraries or abstractions before proving they reduce real complexity.
Guessing product behavior when a short clarification would prevent rework.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan Portfolio Buddy 2 changes while preserving working code and responsive behavior.

faq.question: Does it write code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides planning decisions and implementation criteria before code changes happen.

faq.question: Can it be used outside Portfolio Buddy 2?
faq.answer: Yes, but project-specific examples and Tailwind assumptions may need adaptation.

faq.question: When should it ask clarifying questions?
faq.answer: It should ask when requirements are ambiguous, architectural choices differ, or user experience could change.

faq.question: How does it handle refactoring?
faq.answer: It defaults to preservation and only proposes improvement when risk is low, upside is high, and complexity stays low.

faq.question: Does it include security controls?
faq.answer: It does not add security controls. It supports careful planning, approval, and validation habits.
